name: ResizablePanels
title: Components/Layout/ResizablePanels
description:
`ResizablePanel` inherits `PanelProps` from react-resizable-panels and forwards native div attributes. Size numbers are pixels; explicit strings such as `"35%"` keep proportional layouts.

| ResizablePanel prop | Type | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | `string` or `number` | Generated ID; use stable IDs for saved layouts |
| children | `ReactNode` | Content within the panel |
| defaultSize | `number` or `string` | Shares available space when omitted |
| minSize / maxSize | `number` or `string` | `0%` / `100%` |
| collapsible | `boolean` | Enables collapse below the minimum size |
| collapsedSize | `number` or `string` | `0%` |
| collapsedThreshold | `number` or `string` | Half the gap between collapsedSize and minSize |
| disabled | `boolean` | Prevents direct and indirect resizing |
| groupResizeBehavior | `'preserve-relative-size'` or `'preserve-pixel-size'` | `'preserve-relative-size'` |
| onResize | `(size, id, previousSize) => void` | Sizes contain `asPercentage` and `inPixels` |
| panelRef / elementRef | `Ref<PanelImperativeHandle>` / `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | Imperative panel controls / DOM access |
| className / style | `string` / `CSSProperties` | Native presentation props |

Collapsed panels become inert and hidden from assistive technology. `ResizeHandle` has its own prop table below and supports arrow keys and Enter.
purpose: Let people allocate space to the parts of a workspace they need most.
usage: Compose panels and labeled handles. Percentage strings express proportional sizes; numeric sizes are pixels. Handles support pointer and keyboard input.

props.name: defaultLayout
props.description:
Default layout for the Group.

ℹ️ This value allows layouts to be remembered between page reloads.

⚠️ Slight layout shift may occur when server-rendering panels with percentage-based default sizes.
Refer to the documentation for suggestions on how to minimize the impact of this.

props.name: disableCursor
props.description:
This library sets custom mouse cursor styles to indicate drag state.
Use this prop to disable that behavior for Panels and Separators in this group.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disable resize functionality.

props.name: elementRef
props.description: Ref attached to the root `HTMLDivElement`.

props.name: groupRef
props.description:
Exposes the following imperative API:
- `getLayout(): Layout`
- `setLayout(layout: Layout): void`

ℹ️ The `useGroupRef` and `useGroupCallbackRef` hooks are exported for convenience use in TypeScript projects.

props.name: id
props.description:
Uniquely identifies this group within an application.
Falls back to `useId` when not provided.

ℹ️ This value will also be assigned to the `id` and `data-testid` attributes.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.name: is
props.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

props.name: onLayoutChange
props.description:
Called when the Group's layout is changing.

⚠️ For layout changes caused by pointer events, this method is called each time the pointer is moved.
For most cases, it is recommended to use the `onLayoutChanged` callback instead.

props.name: onLayoutChanged
props.description:
Called after the Group's layout has  been changed.

ℹ️ For layout changes caused by pointer events, this method is not called until the pointer has been released.
This method is recommended when saving layouts to some storage api.

ℹ️ The second argument contains meta information about the layout change.
The `isUserInteraction` attribute signals whether the resize was caused by direct user input.
It is true for resizes caused by pointer or keyboard input
and false for other triggers (e.g. imperative API calls, initial mount, etc.)
The `requestedLayout` attribute is the layout before constraints were applied for the current Group size;
prefer it when persisting layouts.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Specifies the resizable orientation ("horizontal" or "vertical"); defaults to "horizontal"

props.name: resizePreviewMode
props.description:
Controls whether pointer dragging updates `Panel`s sizes immediately,
or renders overlay separator previews until the pointer is released.

Defaults to `"panel"` (immediate resizing); `"separator"` defers resizing until release.

Customize previews using the `SeparatorOverlay` component.

props.name: resizeTargetMinimumSize
props.description:
Minimum size of the resizable hit target area (either `Separator` or `Panel` edge)
This threshold ensures are large enough to avoid mis-clicks.

- Coarse inputs (typically a finger on a touchscreen) have reduced accuracy;
to ensure accessibility and ease of use, hit targets should be larger to prevent mis-clicks.
- Fine inputs (typically a mouse) can be smaller

ℹ️ [Apple interface guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) suggest `20pt` (`27px`) on desktops and `28pt` (`37px`) for touch devices
In practice this seems to be much larger than many of their own applications use though.

props.name: className
props.description:
CSS class name.

⚠️ Class is applied to nested `HTMLDivElement` to avoid styles that interfere with Flex layout.

props.name: collapsedSize
props.description: Panel size when collapsed; defaults to 0%.

props.name: collapsedThreshold
props.description:
Distance a collapsible panel must be resized past its `minSize` to collapse,
or past its `collapsedSize` to expand.
Defaults to half the distance between `collapsedSize` and `minSize`.

For example if a panel declares `collapsedSize="5%"`, `collapsedThreshold="5%"`, and `minSize="25%"`,
it will collapse when resized below 20% and expands when resized above 10%.

ℹ️ Interpretation rules:
- Numbers are interpreted as pixels (e.g. `minSize={200}` is 200 pixels)
- Strings without explicit units are interpreted as percentage (e.g. `minSize="50"` is 50 percent)
- Use explicit units (e.g. "px", "%", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw") to change interpretation

props.name: collapsible
props.description:
This panel can be collapsed.

ℹ️ A collapsible panel will collapse when it's size is less than of the specified `minSize`

props.name: defaultSize
props.description:
Default size of Panel within its parent group; default is auto-assigned based on the total number of Panels.

ℹ️ Interpretation rules:
- Numbers are interpreted as pixels (e.g. `defaultSize={200}` is 200 pixels)
- Strings without explicit units are interpreted as percentage (e.g. `defaultSize="50"` is 50 percent)
- Use explicit units (e.g. "px", "%", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw") to change interpretation

⚠️ Percentage based sizes may cause slight layout shift when server-rendering.
For more information see the documentation.

props.name: disabled
props.description: When disabled, a panel cannot be resized either directly or indirectly (by resizing another panel).

props.name: elementRef
props.description: Ref attached to the root `HTMLDivElement`.

props.name: groupResizeBehavior
props.description:
How should this Panel behave if the parent Group is resized?
Defaults to `preserve-relative-size`.

- `preserve-relative-size`: Retain the current relative size (as a percentage of the Group)
- `preserve-pixel-size`: Retain its current size (in pixels)

ℹ️ Panel min/max size constraints may impact this behavior.

⚠️ A Group must contain at least one Panel with `preserve-relative-size` resize behavior.

props.name: id
props.description:
Uniquely identifies this panel within the parent group.
Falls back to `useId` when not provided.

ℹ️ This prop is used to associate persisted group layouts with the original panel.

ℹ️ This value will also be assigned to the `id` and `data-testid` attributes.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.name: is
props.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

props.name: maxSize
props.description:
Maximum size of Panel within its parent group; defaults to `"100%"`.

ℹ️ Interpretation rules:
- Numbers are interpreted as pixels (e.g. `maxSize={200}` is 200 pixels)
- Strings without explicit units are interpreted as percentage (e.g. `maxSize="50"` is 50 percent)
- Use explicit units (e.g. "px", "%", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw") to change interpretation

props.name: minSize
props.description:
Minimum size of Panel within its parent group; defaults to 0%.

ℹ️ Interpretation rules:
- Numbers are interpreted as pixels (e.g. `minSize={200}` is 200 pixels)
- Strings without explicit units are interpreted as percentage (e.g. `minSize="50"` is 50 percent)
- Use explicit units (e.g. "px", "%", "em", "rem", "vh", or "vw") to change interpretation

props.name: onResize
props.type: ((panelSize: PanelSize, id: string | number | undefined, prevPanelSize: PanelSize | undefined) => void) | undefined
props.description: Called when panel sizes change.

props.name: panelRef
props.description:
Exposes the following imperative API:
- `collapse(): void`
- `expand(): void`
- `getSize(): number`
- `isCollapsed(): boolean`
- `resize(size: number): void`

ℹ️ The `usePanelRef` and `usePanelCallbackRef` hooks are exported for convenience use in TypeScript projects.

props.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowcount
props.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindex
props.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

props.name: aria-rowspan
props.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

props.name: aria-setsize
props.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-sort
props.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

props.name: aria-valuemax
props.description: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuemin
props.description: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuenow
props.description: Defines the current value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

props.name: disabled
props.description:
When disabled, the separator cannot be used to resize its neighboring panels.

ℹ️ The panels may still be resized indirectly (while other panels are being resized).
To prevent a panel from being resized at all, it needs to also be disabled.

props.name: disableDoubleClick
props.description: When true, double-clicking this `Separator` will not reset its `Panel` to its default size.

props.name: elementRef
props.description: Ref attached to the root `HTMLDivElement`.

props.name: id
props.description:
Uniquely identifies the separator within the parent group.
Falls back to `useId` when not provided.

ℹ️ This value will also be assigned to the `id` and `data-testid` attributes.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.name: is
props.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

props.name: preview
props.description: Overrides the `Group` default preview for this `Separator` when `resizePreviewMode` is "separator".

props.name: style
props.description:
